solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe Queen's printed greeting

definitions.meaning: a queen is one example of a playing ..., so 'maybe' marks it as an instance
a birthday or Christmas message on folded stiff paper

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the monarch's festive message comes in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen's' reads as 'Queen is': a queen may be one of a pack of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are nouns for a piece of stiff paper: one from a pack used in games, one sent with good wishes.

clue.text: Spy taking time, not losing heart

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, so the word not drops its centre

explanation.surface: A spy who bides their time without becoming discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes the O from NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret operative working for an intelligence service is a synonym for a spy.

clue.text: Garden site — it's abandoned and decays

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A neglected garden plot left to rot away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' looks like it describes the site, but it signals rearranging the letters of GARDEN SITE ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To break up into fragments and fall apart is a synonym for rotting away or decaying.

clue.text: Planned performance involving Leo maybe

indicators.note: involving means taking something within, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance of something
Leo is one example of a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A staged show with a lion, or someone called Leo, arranged in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leo maybe' is a definition by example: Leo is one of the zodiac's signs, hence the 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drawn up or intended beforehand has been worked out, a synonym for planned.

clue.text: Doctor, individual who is 20?

definitions.note: 20-across is INACTIVE, so this means a person who does nothing

explanation.surface: Asking whether a physician is a twenty-year-old.
explanation.walkthrough: The 20 refers to the answer of 20-across, INACTIVE: a lazy idler.
explanation.definitionFit: A male bee that does no work gives its name to an idle person who lives off others' labour.

clue.text: Fancy new taps that you might want in kitchen

definitions.text: that you might want in kitchen

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or decorative, here telling us to rework these letters

explanation.surface: Smart new taps are the sort of thing a kitchen needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the taps, but it rearranges NEW TAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooking pot for slow simmering is an item a cook would keep in the kitchen.

clue.text: I go to a sad man in distress? That could be about right

definitions.text: I go to a sad man in distress? That could be about right

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around another letter
distress here means damage or disorder, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.words: I go to a sad man

explanation.surface: Someone who helps a man in trouble wonders whether that makes them a kindly helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' rearranges IGOTOASADMAN; 'about' puts those letters around R. The whole clue also describes the parable's helper.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible parable a passing traveller stops to help a robbed and beaten man, so anyone who helps a stranger in trouble earns the name.

clue.text: Unusually rare twitching, lacking predictability

indicators.note: unusually suggests out of the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitching of a muscle

explanation.surface: A strange, irregular twitch that nobody can foresee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges RARE into ERRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that is irregular and unreliable is a synonym for being impossible to foresee.

clue.text: Shoes are awkward where there could be sand

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy or ill-arranged, so these letters must be reordered

explanation.surface: Shoes are uncomfortable in a place full of sand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges SHOES ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The strip of land beside the sea is a beach, a place that is often sandy.

clue.text: Ordinary Seaman crosses a river — boat may need these

indicators.note: crosses here means straddles, so one piece goes either side of the rest

parts.note: OS is the naval abbreviation for an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor rows across a river, needing equipment for the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosses' puts OS around A and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing boat needs poles with flat blades to be pulled through the water.

clue.text: Position of a new church at back of street

indicators.note: at back of means the following pieces come after the street abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Where a newly built church stands behind the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Position' looks like the start of a phrase about the church, but it is the definition; 'at back of' places the church after the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is the way one stands or an opinion one holds, both senses of position.

clue.text: Note some of those turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top
some of means only a part of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A remark about some people who are arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' takes HOS from 'those' and 'turning up' turns it to SOH.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa the fifth step of the scale is a musical note, also spelt sol.

clue.text: Gym group wanting a bit of money, as before

definitions.note: a coin of the former currency of Spain, replaced by the euro

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A gym class that is short of a little cash, just as it was earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as before' marks the currency as no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Spanish currency unit until the euro arrived in 2002, so it is money of the past.

clue.text: Ohio commences new subject for students

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An Ohio school launches a new course for its pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges OHIO COMMENCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookery and household management is a school course, so it is a subject taught to pupils.

clue.text: Work on a product with shimmery colouring

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a line is a range of goods or a product sold

explanation.surface: Working on a product that has a shimmering finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal shows shifting iridescent colours, so something like it in appearance has a shimmering look.

clue.text: Dismiss bank employee

definitions.meaning: to discharge an officer from the armed forces in disgrace
a teller who handles money in a bank

explanation.surface: Fire the teller at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a verb for expelling an officer from service; the other a noun for someone paying out and receiving money.

clue.text: Get depressed, given long account that reaches no conclusion

indicators.note: no conclusion means the final letter is removed from the long story word

parts.note: a saga is a long story or account

explanation.surface: Feeling down after hearing an endless story with no ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that reaches no conclusion' cuts the last A from SAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink or droop downward under weight is to be pressed down, a sense of depressed.

clue.text: One of three men in a boat somewhere in the Outer Hebrides

definitions.text: One of three men in a boat
definitions.meaning: a character in Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat, about a Thames trip
a part of Lewis and ..., an island off north-west Scotland, famous for tweed

explanation.surface: A rower afloat somewhere in the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Three Men in a Boat (1889) is a classic English comic novel; the Outer Hebrides are islands off Scotland's west coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a companion of J and George in the novel and to the southern part of the largest Hebridean island.

clue.text: Passenger finally entering smart train

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one letter is put into the other word

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word passenger

explanation.surface: A passenger at last boards a stylish train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from 'Passenger'; 'entering' puts it inside STING. 'smart' looks like an adjective for the train but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A train can be a series or line of things, such as a string of horses or events.

clue.text: Broken bit that's solid under surface of soil

indicators.note: under means the solid piece sits below the soil's letter in this down entry
the surface of a word is its top, which in a down clue is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fragment of something firm lies buried beneath the topsoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surface of' takes S from 'soil'; 'under' puts HARD below it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp piece of broken pottery or glass is a fragment, a broken bit.

clue.text: New sort of book

explanation.surface: A fresh kind of book.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means original and unfamiliar; as a noun it is a long work of fiction.

clue.text: Opening of pub in time for a beer?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of pub

explanation.surface: Arriving at the pub when it opens, just in time for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening of' takes P from 'pub'. The question mark shows the measure is only one example of a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A common serving of beer in Britain is a measure of about half a litre.

clue.text: When disturbed, I can't — I have to be doing nothing

indicators.note: disturbed means upset from its proper order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone protesting they can't help being idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When disturbed' rearranges I CANT into INACT, followed by IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being idle and not moving or acting is a synonym for doing nothing.

clue.text: Yours truly when terribly rude must be restrained

parts.note: yours truly is a jokey way of saying me
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: terribly suggests badly done, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker admits they must hold back when being very rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges RUDE into URED.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured response is calm and deliberate, a synonym for being held in check.

clue.text: River essential for Egyptian, I learn

indicators.note: essential for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Egyptian learner says the waterway is vital to the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa's great waterway that flows north through Egypt is an example of a river.
